In learning from our city of Saskatoon internal experts, the anti-advocate Dorothea Swift Wolf, an indigenous initiatives director Melissa Cote.
Indigenous peacekeeping is a holistic, culturally grounded and restorative approach that prioritizes trust relationships connectedness and healing.
Indigenous peacekeepers work to address the root cause as a conflict as their primary role.
They are community centered and focused on connecting individuals to appropriate community resources.
The fundamental difference between general security and indigenous peacekeepers is the underlying authority and approach to community safety.
Security, as typically established by government or private companies, is established under institutions and structures and is granted authority via laws, acts and by laws.
Indigenous lead peacekeepers are granted authority through their local leadership community relationships and cultural connections.

Administration believes that both general security supported by laws, acts and by laws and indigenous lead peacekeepers with connections to culture and community are part of overall security coordinated response.
Five options have been presented for your consideration for indigenous lead peacekeepers.
Administration is recommending option for a one-year partnership in a bid area or bid areas.
That would be two indigenous lead peacekeeping teams, so four staff, 12 hours a day, 365 days a year.
